summary: The design fits the existing PageIndex composition, but several contracts are underspecified: catalog rows currently model only books, toolkit discovery is reflection-based, and tree writes span multiple stores. The highest risks are incomplete write authorization, lazy notebook registration races, import atomicity, and relation/anchor consistency across re-indexes.

suggestions.title: Use a separate notebook catalog model or fully separate row contract
suggestions.rationale: `books` currently requires non-null source fields, while `BookCard` requires `source_path`, `source_sha256`, and a book-only `source_format`. Inserting notebook rows into `books` therefore requires sentinel values and causes existing `list_cards`, search, and `resolve_book` paths to treat notebooks as books. A separate `notebooks` table/model, or an explicitly nullable discriminated model with all callers filtering `kind='book'`, is needed before implementation.

suggestions.title: Replace lazy registration with an atomic ownership protocol
suggestions.rationale: The proposed facade reads the catalog for authorization, while notebook rows are created only when Bookstore later reads a matching tree. During that gap, a `<book>_notes` tree is uncatalogued and can be renamed or deleted; concurrent readers can also race to register it. Registration must happen atomically with notebook creation/adoption, or authorization must classify reserved notebook names directly from the catalog and filesystem before dispatch.

suggestions.title: Centralize write authorization and include every mutating operation
suggestions.rationale: `PageIndexToolkit` has mutators beyond the proposed table, notably `index_segments`, and writes occur through both `_mutate` and direct lock/publication paths such as `create_tree`, `delete_tree`, `rename_tree`, and `vacuum_tree`. A manually maintained hook at individual method tops will regress when a new tool is added. Put authorization at a common dispatch/transaction boundary, explicitly cover `index_segments`, and add a test that every mutating public method is either authorized or intentionally excluded.

suggestions.title: Authorize both endpoints of rename operations
suggestions.rationale: `rename_tree` accepts independent `src` and `dst` names and checks the destination during publication. A policy that authorizes only the apparent target can allow an uncatalogued tree to be renamed onto a catalogued book, or a protected book to be moved to an uncatalogued name. The facade must resolve and authorize both endpoints under the same lock/decision snapshot.

suggestions.title: Do not claim protection against the plain PageIndex template without an ownership guard
suggestions.rationale: The packaged `pageindex` template still instantiates plain `PageIndexToolkit` over a configurable directory, and that class exposes all mutators by default. A user can point it at `<library>/trees` and bypass the facade; `doctor` detects damage after the fact but cannot enforce immutability. Either add a filesystem/storage ownership marker honored by the generic toolkit, make the library directory inaccessible to the plain template, or narrow the feature claim to protection only through the new server.

suggestions.title: Preserve PageIndex tool schemas instead of changing list_trees shape
suggestions.rationale: The current `PageIndexToolkit.list_trees()` returns `list[str]`. The proposal says the facade has the same tool surface but also says `list_trees` returns annotated entries, which is a breaking response-schema change. Keep `list_trees` compatible and add a separate scoped/annotated listing tool, then compare facade tool names and signatures against `PageIndexToolkit.get_tools()` in a contract test.

suggestions.title: Test no-LLM filtering on the facade explicitly
suggestions.rationale: MCP filtering uses the toolkit class's `llm_dependent_tools`, while Bookstore internally supplies `_NullAdapter` when no real adapter exists. A facade that omits the exact PageIndex metadata can expose LLM-dependent tools in no-LLM mode or hide deterministic tools. Set and test the same filtered tool set, including `insert_content`, `import_file`, `import_folder`, `search_documents_scoped`, and agentic retrieval.

suggestions.title: Make tree import a staged logical snapshot with a complete identity hash
suggestions.rationale: PageIndex persistence consists of JSON, body blobs, and segment revision files; `NodeContentStore` and `SegmentStore` expose separate rename/delete operations, not a single cross-store copy transaction. Copying those pieces and then writing the catalog can leave partial trees after a crash. Additionally, hashing only the tree JSON does not identify referenced body or segment content. Stage under a destination name, validate all references and the one-document rule, publish atomically, and hash the complete logical snapshot or retain a source snapshot manifest.

suggestions.title: Use collision-safe anchor remapping, not title alone
suggestions.rationale: `PageIndexNode` already carries `doc_id`, `revision`, `span`, and `owned` ranges, while section titles are not unique. Matching anchors by `(doc_id, section title)` can silently attach a footnote to the wrong repeated heading after re-indexing. Persist the old structural position/range or content fingerprint, accept only a unique match, and mark duplicate/ambiguous matches stale; add tests for repeated titles, moved sections, and changed revisions.

suggestions.title: Preserve manual relations during re-index invalidation
suggestions.rationale: The proposed `origin='manual'` edges would be deleted by the current `_invalidate_graph`, which calls `delete_relations(book_id=...)` without an origin filter whenever a book is updated. Existing relation refresh code already demonstrates origin-specific deletion for deterministic, LLM, and community edges. Re-index should invalidate only computed origins, while manual edges remain and are explicitly revalidated when their anchored books disappear.

suggestions.title: Make scope part of notebook/book identity at every read boundary
suggestions.rationale: Bookstore resolves duplicate IDs project-first, but the proposed anchors carry an explicit scope and allow notebooks in either scope to reference books in either scope. `find_books` and annotation lookup keyed only by `book_id` can therefore attach a global annotation to a project book with the same ID or silently mask global classification. Either reject cross-scope ID collisions at registration or use a `(scope, book_id)` identity throughout anchor resolution and result provenance.

suggestions.title: Add concurrency and generation-consistency tests for two-server use
suggestions.rationale: The existing PageIndex generation protocol protects individual tree publication, but Bookstore annotation reads, catalog registration, import adoption, and relation projection span multiple trees and SQLite calls. Tests should run concurrent notebook writes with `read_section`, re-index with anchor remapping, import with a forced failure, and project/global lookups, asserting no torn annotation result, orphan catalog row, or lost manual edge.
